extracted.intended_audience: librarians, authors, publishers, educators, and readers seeking information on the Michael L. Printz Award and its eligibility/selection rules
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the eligibility, selection procedures, and substantive criterion used by the Michael L. Printz Award (an ALA/YALSA young-adult literary prize). Covers age-range definition, eligible formats, publication-window rules, committee composition, and other procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary evaluation criterion — literary merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The year's "best book written for teens, based entirely on its literary merit".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award recognizes the best book for teens based solely on literary merit; the Printz was created as a counterpoint to the Newbery to highlight the most literary works written for a young adult audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'young adult' for the award
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'young adult' refers to readers from ages 12 through 18 for purposes of this award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This age-range definition determines eligibility; books intended for younger children or adults are out of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-fiction, fiction, poetry and anthologies are all eligible to receive the Printz Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is not limited to a single literary form — a broad set of formats is considered for literary merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication-date eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: Books must have been published between January 1 and December 31 of the year preceding the announcement of the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only books published during the full calendar year prior to the award announcement are eligible for that year's prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher designation / intended audience requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles must be designated 'young adult' by its publisher or published for the age range that YALSA defines as 'young adult,' i.e., 12 through 18. Adult books are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility depends on the publisher's designation or demonstrable intended audience; books marketed/positioned as adult are excluded even if they might interest teens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Works of joint authorship or editorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Works of joint authorship or editorship are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative works, edited collections, and multi-author volumes may be considered for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posthumous eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The award may be issued posthumously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A winning or honored work may be by an author who has died prior to the award announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously foreign-published works
rubrics_metrics.description: Books previously published in another country are eligible (presuming an American edition has been published during the period of eligibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A foreign-first publication does not bar eligibility provided a U.S. edition appears within the eligibility calendar year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of winners and Honor Books
rubrics_metrics.description: They award one winner and honor up to four additional titles. Up to four worthy runners-up may be designated Honor Books and three or four have been named every year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each year the committee selects a single Printz Medal winner and may designate up to four Honor Books as runners-up; historically three or four Honors have been named in most years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection committee composition and appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection committee comprises nine YALSA members appointed by the president-elect for a one-year term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A nine-member committee of Young Adult Library Services Association members (with one-year appointments by the ALA president-elect) makes the award decisions; this procedural rule defines who evaluates submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Michael L. Printz Award is sponsored by Booklist magazine; administered by the ALA's young-adult division, the Young Adult Library Services Association (YALSA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsorship and administration identify the organizational home and support for the award; Booklist sponsors while YALSA administers the selection process.
